solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Police unit to probe a principal drug user

indicators.note: a probe goes into something, so the police unit is pushed inside the other letters

parts.note: the principal of a school is its head
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force

explanation.surface: Detectives investigate a leading figure in the drug trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidhead is slang for a habitual taker of LSD, so a drug user.

clue.text: Stop a payment via the telephone

indicators.note: on a phone the words are heard rather than seen, so the sound counts

parts.note: a cost is a payment for something

explanation.surface: Someone halts a transaction by ringing the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and stop them, often aggressively, to speak.

clue.text: Island trade Samoan leader values

parts.note: a deal is a trade or transaction

indicators.note: the leader of the word Samoan is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Pacific trade agreement reflects a Samoan chief's principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are principles or standards held dear, which are one's values.

clue.text: Many will eat slice of Roquefort after hot tart

indicators.note: the many-eating piece comes after the hot letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the letters enclose another

parts.note: a lot means many

indicators.note: only a slice, the first letter, of Roquefort is used

explanation.surface: A crowd devours cheese following a hot pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slice of' gives R, which 'will eat' puts inside A LOT. 'tart' looks like pastry but means a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart is slang for a promiscuous woman or prostitute, an old pejorative sense.

clue.text: Corrupt deal utter shambles, article claimed

indicators.note: the anagram claims the article, taking it in
a shambles is a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dishonest agreement is a complete mess, a newspaper piece asserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shambles' rearranges DEAL UTTER; 'claimed' takes A into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate something is to make it impure by adding inferior substances, so to corrupt it.

clue.text: Fine player that contributes to final result

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a player on stage is an actor

explanation.surface: A good performer is a key element in a production's outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is one element or circumstance among several that brings about an outcome.

clue.text: Water mother gets in a market

indicators.note: the mother gets inside the other letters

parts.note: a sale is a market event where goods are sold
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A mother buys a drink at a stall.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a jocular old name for drinking water, as the only drink Adam had.

clue.text: Somehow flirting is of little importance

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are made into the answer in some new way

explanation.surface: Flirtation is in some way inconsequential.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifling means trivial or insignificant, a direct synonym of the phrase.

clue.text: Grass with criminal past put inside, becomes this?

indicators.note: the criminal past is placed inside the grass letters

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
form is British slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: An informer with a record who is jailed turns over a new leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for an informer and 'put inside' for jailed, so the whole clue reads as an informer going straight in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner who has given up crime is said to have changed for the better, the hoped-for outcome.

clue.text: Smack around the lughole? Get off!

indicators.note: the smack goes round the outside of the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a clout is a smack or blow
lughole is British slang for the ear

explanation.surface: Someone threatens a clip round the ear and tells a pest to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are brusque commands telling someone to leave at once: an idiomatic equivalence.

clue.text: Row over heartless administrator's fee

indicators.note: here the row is spread over, covering, the other letters so that they sit inside it

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel or row

indicators.note: with its heart gone, only the outside letters of the word administrator are left

explanation.surface: A dispute arises over the charge levied by an uncaring official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips administrator to its outside letters, A and R, which go inside TIFF after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of charges, so a fee or rate to be paid.

clue.text: French article about hooligans and betrayers

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the article is read backwards

parts.note: les is the French plural definite article
louts are rough, uncouth hooligans

explanation.surface: A French news piece covers football thugs and traitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sells out abandons principles or comrades for gain, so is a traitor.

clue.text: Army loses head with half-cut bugler, a stable man once

indicators.note: the army word drops its first letter, its head

parts.note: a host is an army or great multitude

indicators.note: only half of bugler is kept, its back half

explanation.surface: A drunken bugler costs the army its commander, in a tale of an old stableman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' makes HOST into OST; 'half-cut' keeps LER, the back half of BUGLER. Half-cut is also British slang for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostler was a groom at an inn who looked after travellers' horses, an old-fashioned job.

clue.text: Terribly cold saunas? That's shocking!

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly treated and shaken into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone complains that freezing saunas are an outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandalous and shocking both describe conduct that causes public outrage: synonyms.

clue.text: Peace pact broken by angry uncle's hostility

indicators.note: the pact is broken open and the other letters are put into the gap

parts.note: a truce is an agreement to stop fighting

indicators.note: angry letters are agitated and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A ceasefire collapses because of an irate relative's aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angry' signals the anagram, CULEN, and 'broken by' splits the pact to take it; the surface makes 'angry' describe the uncle.
explanation.definitionFit: Truculence is aggressive defiance, an eagerness to fight, which is hostility.

clue.text: Retired old man with little desire for sex?

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: pa is a father, one's old man
petite means small or little

explanation.surface: A pensioner with a dwindling libido.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is narrowed to one kind of craving.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite is a craving, and sexual appetite is a common phrase, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Bird food

definitions.meaning: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, as is the word in the answer
a breakfast dish of oats boiled in water or milk

explanation.surface: Seed fed to birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is oatmeal cooked in milk, and also British slang for time served in prison.

clue.text: Some game husband's left out for country folk

indicators.note: the husband letter is left out of the game birds

parts.note: pheasants are game birds
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A shooting party's husband misses out on the birds meant for the villagers.
explanation.definitionFit: Peasants are rural farm labourers, people of the countryside.

clue.text: New transept houses holy books for pious type

indicators.note: the anagram gives the books a home, holding them inside
new letters are a fresh arrangement of the original word

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the first books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A newly built part of a church holds scripture for a devout worshipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' signals the anagram, PRESTANT, which 'houses' the holy books; 'New' reads as if it went with Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A Protestant is a member of a Western Christian church, here loosely a religious person.

clue.text: Sort of shield

definitions.meaning: to sort is to sift or vet, as in vetting candidates

explanation.surface: A kind of protective shield.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen is to sift and also to shelter something from view or harm.

clue.text: Non-Equity production shot in the morning?

parts.note: am stands for the morning hours
a dram is a shot of whisky

explanation.surface: A film made by amateurs is shot early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the British actors' union, so a non-Equity show uses amateurs.
explanation.definitionFit: Am-dram is amateur dramatics, theatre by performers who are not union professionals.

clue.text: Harmony in marriage is scarce, primarily

indicators.note: in marriage is read as the scarce letter sitting inside the marriage word

parts.note: a marriage is a union

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the first letter of scarce

explanation.surface: Domestic bliss is rare in wedlock, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means in agreement, so the word means harmony or accord.

clue.text: Going out, say, on ship

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here
re means on or about, as in a letter
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A traveller explains how they will leave: by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Egress is the act of exiting, a noun matching the gerund sense of departing.

clue.text: Sort of cake old lady's given to new lover

parts.note: a fancy is a small iced cake
old lady is slang for one's mother, ma

explanation.surface: An older woman hands a pastry to her young boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy man is a woman's paramour, often an illicit one: an old-fashioned idiom.

clue.text: I eat after ten

indicators.note: the eating word follows the number in the answer

parts.note: ten written in figures is 10, read as the letters I and O
to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Someone announces a late dinner time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker; it is the definition, the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: I is the chemical symbol of the element with atomic number 53.

clue.text: I forage around woods ultimately to find delicacy

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved about and put in a new order
ultimately takes the final letter of woods

explanation.surface: A forager searches the forest for a gourmet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives S, the end of woods, which joins IFORAGE in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Foie gras, fattened goose or duck liver, is a luxury French food.

clue.text: Tip of elbow nurse must keep very, very still

indicators.note: the first letters hold the next one inside them
the tip of the word elbow is its first letter

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
so means very, as in so tired

explanation.surface: A nurse tells a patient to keep an injured arm absolutely motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip of' and 'must keep' build EVEN; the repeated 'very' is two different abbreviations. 'still' reads as motionless but means nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so and still both mean nevertheless, an idiomatic synonym of the adverb.

clue.text: When servant's punched by old knight and earl together

indicators.note: a hole is punched in the first letters and the others are knocked into it

parts.note: as means when, as in as he left
a man is a manservant
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A servant is assaulted by an elderly aristocrat and his companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting as one man means everyone acting in unison, all together.
